why: Every command in both briefs should run as written. The builder brief names bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js, package.json and README.md, and all five are tracked at this commit. It uses `npm test`, which package.json defines. It avoids the issue's nonexistent `npm run test:cli`. Its JS string '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n' correctly gives literal backslash-t escapes. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is only README text, not a step to run. In the verifier brief, each `printf ... | node bin/csv2json.js [--tsv] > /tmp/oN; printf '%s\n' '...' > /tmp/eN; cmp ... && echo SAME` is valid shell. In Check 5, `%s` with single quotes keeps \t as two literal characters, which matches JSON.stringify's escaping. `echo "exit=$?"` after a pipeline reports node's exit status. `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*` and `cat README.md` are valid.
